formation.title: The Kingdom Restored
formation.text:
The old Kingdom of Burgundy, the Kingdom of Arles, lives again. For centuries this realm existed only as a memory, its lands fragmented between French kings, Savoyard dukes, and Imperial pretenders. Now a single crown unites the Rhone valley from the Alpine passes to the Mediterranean shore, from the vineyards of Provence to the salt works of the Jura.

But what kind of kingdom shall this be? The Rhone corridor stretches south toward the sea, a natural highway for commerce and culture. Avignon's papal legacy and the troubadour courts offer a path of refinement, trade, and Mediterranean sophistication. Alternatively, our Alpine heartland gives us command of every pass between France and Italy: a toll-master's paradise and a mountain fortress that no army can easily breach.

The choice will define our dynasty.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: The Rhone is our highway. Let wine and song flow south to the sea.

modifiers.name: The Rhone Corridor
modifiers.text: From Avignon to Lyon, the Rhone is our great artery, carrying wine, silk, and culture to the wider world. We are heirs to the troubadours and the papal court, a civilization that prizes beauty, learning, and the art of living well.

options.text: We are the gatekeepers of the Alps. None shall pass without our leave.

modifiers.name: Alpine Gatekeepers
modifiers.text: We command the high passes where armies and merchants alike must pay our toll. The mountains are our ramparts, the cols our gates. What crosses the Alps crosses at our pleasure, and every mule train that descends to Italy enriches our treasury.

advances.name: Troubadour Courts
advances.text: The courts of Provence and the Rhone valley gave birth to the troubadour tradition: the first major body of secular lyric poetry in a vernacular European language, celebrating courtly love, chivalric virtue, and the refinement of the Occitan-speaking nobility.

advances.name: Alpine Toll Mastery
advances.text: Control of key alpine passes (the Great Saint Bernard, Mont Cenis, and the Simplon) allows the collection of tolls on every merchant caravan, pilgrim column, and military expedition crossing between France and Italy.

advances.name: Rhone Viticulture
advances.text: The Rhone valley's sun-drenched terraces have produced wine since Roman times. Monastic communities refined the art of viticulture across the centuries, creating a tradition that would eventually produce some of Europe's finest vintages.

advances.name: Montagnard Tradition
advances.text: The Savoyard mountain cavalry, hardy riders bred in alpine valleys, are uniquely adapted to rough terrain where lowland horsemen founder. They serve as scouts, raiders, and pass defenders.

advances.name: Arpitan Identity
advances.text: The Arpitan and Occitan linguistic traditions unite the diverse peoples of the Burgundian-Provencal realm, from the Franco-Provencal speakers of the Alpine valleys to the Provencal troubadours of the Mediterranean coast.

advances.name: Comital Courts
advances.text: The comital courts of Savoy established a tradition of centralized administration that would endure for centuries, with the counts and later dukes maintaining effective jurisdiction across their fragmented Alpine domains.

advances.name: Avignon Legacy
advances.text: The seventy years of the Avignon papacy (1309-1377) left an indelible mark on Provence: the Palais des Papes, the artistic traditions of Simone Martini and Matteo Giovannetti, and a cosmopolitan scholarly culture that persisted long after the popes returned to Rome.

event.title: The Legacy of the Papal Court
event.text:
For seventy years, the popes made Avignon the center of Christendom. Though the Holy See returned to Rome in 1377, the imprint of papal patronage on Provence is indelible. The Palais des Papes still towers over the Rhone, the largest Gothic palace in Europe: a monument to the artistic ambitions of Popes Clement V, John XXII, and their successors.

Under papal patronage, Simone Martini brought Sienese painting to Avignon. Matteo Giovannetti covered chapel walls with intricate frescoes. The papal library became one of Europe's finest. Pope John XXII planted the vineyards of Chateauneuf-du-Pape and refined the viticulture of the entire region.

This legacy of artistic and intellectual patronage remains a wellspring for our court.

options.text: We shall be worthy inheritors of the papal legacy.

modifiers.name: Papal Patronage
modifiers.text: The legacy of the Avignon papacy endures in our courts: a tradition of ecclesiastical splendor, artistic commissioning, and scholarly inquiry that elevates our realm above its neighbors.

advances.name: Chateauneuf-du-Pape
advances.text: Pope John XXII planted the vineyards that would bear his castle's name, Chateauneuf-du-Pape. By 1344, nearly half the surrounding land was devoted to viticulture, producing wines that rivaled the finest in Europe. The papal imprimatur elevated Rhone winemaking to an art.

advances.name: Grande Saline
advances.text: The salt works of Salins-les-Bains in Franche-Comte: one of Europe's largest industrial complexes, producing 14,000 tons of salt per year and employing over 800 workers. This white gold fed half of eastern France and the Swiss cantons.

event.title: The White Gold of Salins
event.text:
The Grande Saline of Salins-les-Bains has produced salt for over a thousand years. In the medieval period, it became the economic capital of Franche-Comte, eight hundred workers laboring in its vast underground galleries to extract brine from wells plunging deep into the Jurassic bedrock. The salt fed Burgundy, Franche-Comte, and half the Swiss cantons.

The salines generate half the region's income. Control of this white gold gives us leverage over our neighbors and a reliable source of wealth that neither war nor famine can easily disrupt. We would be wise to expand and modernize our salt works.

options.text: The salines are the treasury of our kingdom.

modifiers.name: Salt Monopoly
modifiers.text: The white gold of Franche-Comte flows from our salines to feed half of Europe. This monopoly on nature's most essential commodity fills our coffers and binds neighboring cantons to our trade.

advances.name: Savoyard Chancery
advances.text: The administrative apparatus of the Savoyard state: a professional chancery staffed by trained scribes and notaries who maintained the legal and diplomatic machinery of a realm that straddled the Alps.

advances.name: Provencal Galleys
advances.text: The ports of Marseille and Toulon launched galleys that patrolled the western Mediterranean, defending Provencal trade routes and projecting power along the coast from the Rhone delta to the Ligurian shore.

advances.name: Burgundian Drill
advances.text: The military reforms of the Burgundian dukes emphasized regular drill, standardized equipment, and disciplined formations: innovations that transformed the medieval host into something approaching a professional army.

advances.name: Ordonnance Reform
advances.text: The companies of ordonnance: permanent military formations of 900 men organized into combined-arms squadrons of men-at-arms, archers, pikemen, and handgunners. First established by Charles the Bold's ordinances of 1471-1473, they represent a revolution in European military organization.

event.title: The Ordonnance Companies
event.text:
Following the example of the Burgundian dukes, we have published detailed military ordinances standardizing the equipment, training, and organization of our soldiers. The old feudal host, where each lord brought whatever men he could muster in whatever arms they possessed, gives way to companies of ordonnance: permanent formations of men-at-arms, archers, pikemen, and handgunners operating under a unified chain of command.

Each company of nine hundred men is organized into squadrons, with heavy cavalry supported by mounted archers and foot soldiers in disciplined combined-arms formations. Uniforms, standardized weapons, and regular drill transform a feudal rabble into a professional force.

options.text: Discipline and organization shall be our strength.

advances.name: Rhone Trade System
advances.text: The Rhone serves as a natural commercial highway linking the Mediterranean to the heart of France. Riverine commerce, fair privileges, and established trade networks make the Rhone valley one of the most prosperous corridors in western Europe.

advances.name: Mountain Fortresses
advances.text: The bastilles of Savoy, stone fortresses commanding alpine passes and valley choke points, make any invasion of the realm a nightmare of siege warfare in hostile terrain.

advances.name: Literary Renaissance
advances.text: The literary traditions of Provence undergo a renaissance, with courts patronizing scholars, poets, and early printers who disseminate knowledge in both Latin and the Occitan vernacular.

advances.name: Order of the Annunciation
advances.text: The Supreme Order of the Most Holy Annunciation, founded by Amadeus VI of Savoy in 1362, ranks among Europe's most prestigious chivalric orders. Membership binds the highest nobility to the Savoyard cause and enhances diplomatic prestige across Christendom.

advances.name: Silk Workshops
advances.text: The introduction of silk weaving to the Rhone valley, initially under Italian influence, would eventually make Lyon one of Europe's great silk centers. The craft demands skill, capital, and access to raw silk from the East.

advances.name: Confessional Crossroads
advances.text: Positioned between Catholic France, Reformed Geneva, and the confessionally divided Empire, the Burgundian-Provencal realm must navigate the wars of religion with pragmatic tolerance or decisive alignment.

advances.name: Savoyard Infantry
advances.text: Professional Savoyard infantry, trained in the pike-and-shot tradition and influenced by both Italian condottiere and Burgundian ordonnance methods, form the backbone of the standing army.

advances.name: Centralized Administration
advances.text: A centralized administrative apparatus, centered on the capital at Chambery, brings coherent governance to the diverse territories of the realm, from Alpine valleys to Mediterranean ports.

advances.name: Toll Modernization
advances.text: Standardization of the toll and customs system across all alpine passes and Rhone river crossings, replacing the patchwork of local tolls with a rational revenue system that maximizes income while reducing friction for established merchants.

advances.name: Marseille Port
advances.text: Expansion of the naval facilities at Marseille transforms the ancient port into a proper arsenal capable of building and maintaining warships for Mediterranean operations.

advances.name: University Tradition
advances.text: The University of Avignon, founded in 1303, and other institutions of learning across the realm cultivate a tradition of legal and theological scholarship that sustains administrative competence and intellectual vitality.

advances.name: Absolutist State
advances.text: Centralization of royal authority on the French model, consolidating the patchwork of feudal jurisdictions, autonomous communes, and ecclesiastical liberties into a unified absolutist state.

advances.name: Standing Army
advances.text: Professionalization of the army into a permanent standing force of line infantry, replacing the seasonal levies and mercenary companies of earlier centuries with year-round soldiers trained in modern drill.

advances.name: Fortress Modernization
advances.text: Modernization of the Alpine fortress network along Vauban principles: star forts with angled bastions replacing the medieval curtain walls, updated to withstand artillery bombardment.

advances.name: Wine Appellations
advances.text: Codification of wine production standards and regional appellations, a precursor to the modern AOC system that would become France's gift to viticulture. Quality control and geographic designation protect the reputation and value of Burgundian and Provencal wines.

advances.name: Arsenal Expansion
advances.text: Expansion of Mediterranean naval capacity with the construction of frigates for trade protection and coastal patrol, establishing a proper naval force to secure Provencal maritime interests.

advances.name: Salon Culture
advances.text: The Enlightenment arrives in the salons of Lyon, Avignon, and Chambery (gatherings of philosophers, scientists, and literary figures) who debate natural philosophy, political reform, and the rights of man.

advances.name: Modern Viticulture
advances.text: Proto-industrial methods transform wine production from an artisanal craft into a systematic industry: large estates employing modern agricultural techniques, controlled fermentation, and organized export networks.

advances.name: Constitutional Reform
advances.text: Representative governance and constitutional principles replace absolutist rule, establishing legislative assemblies, codified rights, and administrative rationalization across the kingdom.

advances.name: Citizen Levy
advances.text: The Chasseurs Alpins, elite mountain infantry recruited from the hardy populations of the Alpine valleys, trained for warfare in the most demanding terrain in Europe.

advances.name: Alpine Infrastructure
advances.text: Modern road and tunnel construction through the Alps: engineering feats that reduce the isolation of mountain valleys and accelerate the flow of commerce across the kingdom's most formidable natural barriers.

advances.name: National Consciousness
advances.text: A distinct Burgundian-Provencal national identity emerges (neither wholly French nor Italian nor Swiss) but a unique Mediterranean-Alpine civilization rooted in troubadour poetry, wine culture, mountain independence, and the memory of the ancient Kingdom of Arles.

destiny.name: The Kingdom of Arles Reborn
destiny.text: The ancient Kingdom of Burgundy lives again. With stability secured, the new realm must choose its path forward: whether to embrace the Mediterranean world or to master the Alpine passes.

event.title: The Kingdom Restored
event.text: The crown of the Kingdom of Arles sits upon our brow once more. What was sundered by centuries of division is now reunited: from the Alpine peaks to the shores of the Mediterranean, the kingdom lives again. History watches to see what we shall make of this inheritance.

destiny.name: Rhone Commerce
destiny.text: Extend the Rhone corridor's commercial reach westward to Montpellier, securing the Languedoc coast and establishing silk as a staple of our capital's trade. Requires 1000 gold in the treasury.

children.text: Silk is produced in the market
Silk is traded in the market

event.title: The Rhone Flows South
event.text: Our merchants and galleys now ply a route that stretches from Lyon to Montpellier and beyond. The Rhone corridor is becoming what nature always intended it to be: a commercial highway linking the heart of Europe to the Mediterranean. Silk from the East arrives in our markets; wine from our vineyards flows outward to every port. The revenue is already transforming our kingdom.

destiny.name: Mare Nostrum
destiny.text: Seize Genoa, the jewel of Mediterranean trade, and integrate its mercantile networks into our growing commercial empire. Marseille, the old Phocaean harbour of our own coast, is built up beside it until the two ports answer each other across the Ligurian Sea. Requires Marseille at 45 development and prestige of 50.

conditions.text: We own Marseille and its development is at least 45

event.title: Genoa Under Our Banner
event.text:
The Superb Republic (La Superba) is ours. Genoa's banking houses, its fleets, its far-flung trading posts from the Black Sea to the Atlantic now serve our crown. The Genoese merchant princes, pragmatic as ever, are already adapting to our rule. The question is how best to exploit this windfall.

We could integrate Genoa's trade networks into a unified Levantine commerce system, channeling eastern goods through our ports. Alternatively, we could build upon Genoa's naval traditions to establish our own thalassocracy: a maritime power that commands respect on every sea.

modifiers.name: Levantine Routes
modifiers.text: The integration of Genoese trade networks channels eastern goods through Provencal ports, enriching our realm with raw materials from across the Mediterranean.

options.text: Build a naval power to rival any on the sea.

modifiers.name: Provencal Thalassocracy
modifiers.text: Our naval forces dominate the western Mediterranean, securing trade routes and projecting power from Catalonia to the Ligurian coast.

destiny.name: The Grand Emporium
destiny.text: Bring Barcelona under our banner, completing our dominion over the western Mediterranean's richest ports. Build a merchants' quarter in Barcelona, the city of the Llotja de Mar, amass 3000 gold and achieve prestige of 75.

conditions.text: Barcelona is owned and has Merchants Quarters, a Grand Marketplace or a Commerce Center

event.title: The Grand Emporium of the West
event.text:
Barcelona, Genoa, Marseille, Montpellier, the greatest ports of the western Mediterranean, fly our banner. Our kingdom has become what the Romans once dreamed of: a single commercial civilization stretching along the entire northern Mediterranean coast. Goods flow from three continents through our harbors.

This unprecedented commercial power can be directed toward building: investing in infrastructure, reducing costs, and creating a prosperous realm. Or it can fuel a cultural renaissance that would make the troubadours weep with joy: a flowering of arts, diplomacy, and influence that cements our place among the great powers of Europe.

options.text: Build the greatest trading realm in Christendom.

modifiers.name: Grand Emporium
modifiers.text: The kingdom has become the greatest commercial hub of the western Mediterranean: a vast trading realm where money flows freely and construction costs are minimal.

options.text: Let our courts rival Florence and Rome.

modifiers.name: Troubadour Renaissance
modifiers.text: A cultural flowering worthy of the troubadour tradition: our courts attract artists, diplomats, and scholars, and our cultural influence radiates across Europe.

destiny.name: Alpine Mastery
destiny.text: Extend our control over the Swiss cantons by taking Zurich, the key to central Switzerland. Maintain an army of at least 30 thousand men and stability of 25.

event.title: Master of the Passes
event.text: Zurich has fallen to our forces. The Swiss cantons now look to our crown rather than to their fractious confederacy. With this conquest, we command the full breadth of the Alpine barrier: every major pass from the Simplon to the Saint Gotthard answers to our toll collectors and our garrisons. No army crosses the mountains without our knowledge; no merchant crosses without paying our due.

options.text: The Alps are our fortress and our treasury.

destiny.name: Piedmont Control
destiny.text: Cross the Alps and seize Turin, the gateway to the Italian peninsula. Build an army of 50 thousand men and hold at least half of Piedmont, so that the plain below the passes is ours and not only its capital.

conditions.text: We hold at least 50% of the locations in Piedmont

event.title: The Descent into Italy
event.text:
Turin is ours. The Savoyard dream of ruling both slopes of the Alps has been realized: we command the passes from above and the Piedmontese plain below. The rich cities of northern Italy lie open before us, their wealth a temptation to any ambitious prince.

Our garrison commanders advocate for a system of iron discipline: fortified positions, rapid reinforcement, and an army that recovers from setbacks faster than any rival. Others counsel a different approach: using our strategic position to extract concessions through diplomacy backed by the threat of force, making every peace treaty and every casus belli serve our expansion.

options.text: Discipline and swift reinforcement are our strengths.

modifiers.name: Iron Garrison
modifiers.text: Our mountain garrisons are paragons of military discipline: rapid reinforcement and high morale recovery make our defensive positions all but unbreakable.

options.text: Strategic position is our greatest weapon.

modifiers.name: Toll Imperium
modifiers.text: Our strategic position astride the Alpine passes gives us unrivaled diplomatic leverage, turning every negotiation and every casus belli to our advantage.

destiny.name: Alpine Hegemony
destiny.text: Take Milan, the richest city of northern Italy, completing our domination of both sides of the Alps. Hold the passes as the porters of the Alps did, with a Col Toll House in four places, field 75 thousand men and achieve prestige of 75.

conditions.text: Has a Col Toll House in at least 4 locations

event.title: The Alpine Imperium
event.text:
Milan (the beating heart of Lombardy, the richest city north of Rome) bows to our crown. We have achieved what no power since Charlemagne has managed: a single realm commanding both the Alpine barrier and the Lombard plain, straddling the great divide between northern and southern Europe.

This hegemony can take the form of military supremacy: an aggressive posture that exploits our strategic position to annex territory and project force across the continent. Alternatively, we can consolidate our mountain kingdom into an impregnable and self-sufficient realm, integrating conquered peoples and building logistical networks that make our armies tireless.

options.text: We are conquerors. Let Italy tremble.

modifiers.name: Alpine Imperator
modifiers.text: An aggressive military posture exploiting our Alpine position: our armies conquer swiftly, annex cheaply, and extract tribute from the vanquished.

options.text: Consolidate our mountain realm into fortress.

modifiers.name: Mountain Kingdom
modifiers.text: An impregnable mountain realm where conquered peoples are swiftly integrated, supply lines run efficiently, and the harsh alpine environment strengthens rather than weakens our forces.

units.name: Montagnard Cavalry
units.text: Hardy Savoyard horsemen from the Alpine valleys, bred to mountain paths where lowland cavalry cannot operate. They serve as scouts, pass defenders, and raiders in the high country.

units.name: Ordonnance Lance
units.text: Professional combined-arms cavalry companies organized according to Burgundian military ordinances. Each lance comprises men-at-arms, archers, and supporting infantry operating as a disciplined combined-arms unit.

units.name: Savoyard Tercios
units.text: Professional Savoyard pike-and-shot infantry, combining Italian tactical sophistication with Burgundian organizational discipline. Trained for both open battle and mountain warfare.

units.name: Line Infantry
units.text: Standing army professional soldiers drilled in modern linear tactics, forming the reliable backbone of the kingdom's military.

units.name: Chasseurs Alpins
units.text: Elite mountain infantry: light, fast, and ruthlessly effective in Alpine terrain. Recruited from the hardiest mountain populations, they are the finest mountain troops in Europe.

units.name: Provencal Galley
units.text: Agile Mediterranean war galleys built in the ports of Provence, faster than standard galleys and optimized for coastal operations in the western Mediterranean.

units.name: Provencal Frigate
units.text: Fast patrol frigates designed for Mediterranean trade protection, capable of intercepting pirates and enforcing Provencal maritime interests along the coast.

buildings.name: Cort d'Amor
buildings.text: A court of love where troubadours perform their cansos and tensons, noble ladies adjudicate questions of courtly devotion, and the refined literary culture of the Occitan world flourishes under aristocratic patronage.

buildings.name: Col Toll House
buildings.text: A fortified customs post at an alpine pass, where every merchant caravan, pilgrim train, and military column must halt and pay the toll before continuing their journey across the mountains.

buildings.name: Vignoble
buildings.text: A terraced vineyard in the sun-drenched Rhone valley, on slopes that have known the vine since Roman times. Its vignerons stake, prune and terrace the slopes, and the land bears more wine.

where.text: The location's raw material is Wine

buildings.name: Palais des Papes
buildings.text: The largest Gothic palace in Europe, built for the Avignon popes. Its soaring chambers, frescoed chapels, and vast library embody the cultural ambitions of the medieval papacy and continue to inspire ecclesiastical and scholarly endeavor.

buildings.name: Saline
buildings.text: A salt extraction works, underground galleries channeling natural brine to the surface, where it is evaporated in great cauldrons over wood fires. The white gold of Franche-Comte has fed eastern France for a millennium.

where.text: Salt is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Chancery
buildings.text: The administrative heart of Savoyard governance: a professional chancery where trained notaries draft laws, maintain records, and manage the diplomatic correspondence of the realm.

buildings.name: Bastille Savoyarde
buildings.text: A formidable mountain fortress built to command an alpine valley or pass, its thick stone walls and commanding position making it all but impervious to assault in an age before heavy artillery.

buildings.name: Silk Workshop
buildings.text: A workshop for the weaving of silk into fine cloth, drawing on techniques introduced from Italy and raw silk imported from the East. The beginning of what would become one of Europe's great textile industries.

buildings.name: Provencal Arsenal
buildings.text: A Mediterranean naval arsenal, shipyard, timber stores, rope walks, and dry docks for the construction and repair of warships that defend Provencal maritime trade.

buildings.name: Grand Domaine
buildings.text: A modern wine estate that takes the place of the old vineyard: drained and replanted slopes, chosen vines and systematic cultivation make the land bear more wine than the vignerons ever drew from it.

where.text: The location's raw material is Wine

buildings.name: Maison de Commerce
buildings.text: A grand Mediterranean trading house: a combined warehouse, exchange, and counting house that serves as the nerve center of our commercial empire, channeling goods and gold from across the sea.

buildings.name: Alpine Citadel
buildings.text: An impregnable mountain fortress complex commanding a strategic Alpine valley: multiple defensive rings, deep magazines, and fortifications designed to withstand the heaviest artillery. The crowning achievement of Burgundian-Provencal military engineering.

list.name: Order of the Golden Fleece
list.text: Founded by Philip the Good at Bruges on 10 January 1430 to celebrate his marriage to Isabella of Portugal, with the permanent seat fixed at Dijon in 1432. The Order's twenty-four (later thirty, then fifty) knights swear personal fealty to the duke and arbitrate their disputes only at the chapter; its annual feasts of Saint Andrew bind the high nobility of every Burgundian land into a single chivalric body. While maintained, it is the most prestigious chivalric order in Christendom; while neglected, its pretensions cost more in burgher subsidy than they purchase in noble loyalty.

list.name: Chambre des Comptes de Dijon
list.text: The ducal audit chamber, formalised by Philip the Bold's ordinance of 11 July 1386 and housed beside the palace from 1460. The auditors (the gens des comptes) register every letter of gift, every office provision, and every alienation of the domain before it can take effect; their professional staff form a literate bourgeois service class running on registers and double-entry. Survives every regime change from 1386 to 1791. Available wherever Dijon is held.

list.name: Estates of Burgundy
list.text: The provincial estates (clergy, nobility, and chartered Bonnes Villes) meeting in regular session since the homage of 1361 and consenting to taxation as the don gratuit. Their voting commissions, the Elus generaux, administer what they grant. The Burgundian, Comtois, Provencal, and Dauphinois assemblies each retain their own constitution. The realm functions as a pays d'etats, prosperous and loyal so long as its consent is asked; mutinous and separatist when it is not.

list.name: Vigueries of Provence
list.text: Inherited from Carolingian local justice and consolidated by Charles I of Anjou after 1246, the Provencal vigueries delegate civil and criminal jurisdiction to an annually-rotated viguier, an assessor judge, and a clavaire-treasurer in each chartered town. The system is the comital footprint in every market town from Aix to Hyeres, bypassing the seigneurial castles. Codified by the surveys of 1252, 1298, and 1333, it survives intact into the French royal apparatus after 1481.

conditions.text: Has primary or accepted culture is Provençal

list.name: Apostolic Camera of Avignon
list.text: The papal financial apparatus reorganised by John XXII after 1316, with more than 650 salaried officials handling annates, servitia, and the procurations of legates from a city of clerks. The Palais des Papes archive, the Rota's appellate machinery, and the partnerships with the Bardi, Peruzzi, and Spini banking houses persist long after the curia returns to Rome in 1377. Whichever realm holds Avignon inherits Christendom's most centralised church bureaucracy.

list.name: Lyon Trade Fairs
list.text: Louis XI's letters of August 1463 fixed Lyon's four annual fairs (Epiphany, Easter, the August Fair, All Saints) as the kingdom's privileged commercial franchise, deliberately diverting trade from Geneva. The Conservation des Foires (a royal judicial commission with abridged appellate procedure) protects merchants, enforces bills of exchange across borders, and makes the August Fair the clearing house for rentes and war loans. By the 1530s the Capponi, Strozzi, and Gondi banks make Lyon a hinge of the European payments system.

list.name: Grande Saunerie de Salins
list.text: The salt monopoly of the Jurassic brine wells at Salins-les-Bains, under comital control since Jean de Chalon-Arlay acquired the barony in 1237. Charles the Bold consolidated the Petite Saline's 419 shares between 1463 and 1477; the Habsburgs completed the buy-out in 1571. By 1590 the saunerie generates 60 per cent of the County of Burgundy's domain revenue. Its gabelous, fortified halls, and standing inspectorate are a state apparatus in miniature: the most lucrative single regalian right in the realm.
